Symbolically, the meeting was unprecedented, but in substance it produced modest results: Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping, and Donald Trump talked for an hour and a half and adopted a declaration that touches on several important issues but sticks to general language. Commentators concluded that the summit was no repeat of the 1945 Yalta Conference, where the leaders of the Soviet Union, Britain, and the United States divided postwar Europe into spheres of influence.
